data.title: NYT Reports Suspicious Prediction Market Bets Before Poll Releases
data.description:
Suspicious prediction market bets were placed shortly before two recent New York Times/Siena political polls became public, according to a report. According to Cointelegraph, Vanderbilt University researchers said a Polymarket user wagered almost $200,000 on Oct. 31 that Nebraska Senator Pete Ricketts would be re-elected, and a Times/Siena poll released an hour later showed Ricketts in the lead. A Friday report by The New York Times said it was unclear whether the user had access to inside information, but the bettor won more than $77,000. The user also placed similar large bets on other markets, including Kalshi. Brett Goldstein of the Vanderbilt Institute of National Security said the circumstances were difficult to dismiss as random and required further investigation. Polymarket said it had identified the trades and was investigating, while Kalshi declined to comment.

Cointelegraph reported in April that a US Army soldier had been charged after allegedly earning more than $400,000 by betting on a prediction market using nonpublic information connected to a US operation involving then Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. The Department of Justice alleged that Master Sergeant Gannon Ken Van Dyke participated in planning and carrying out Operation Absolute Resolve, which led to Maduro’s capture at a residence in Caracas, Venezuela, in January. According to the DOJ, Van Dyke allegedly used that information to purchase “yes” shares in Polymarket contracts tied to the operation, including “Maduro out by January 31” and “Trump invokes War Powers against Venezuela by January 31.” The cases involve separate prediction market activity, and the report did not establish whether the bets made ahead of the Times/Siena poll releases relied on inside information. Polymarket said its investigation into the trades was ongoing.

data.title: HyperCore Sets Minimum USDC Transfer From HyperEVM at 1 USDC
data.description: Hyperliquid News said the minimum amount for transferring USDC from HyperEVM to HyperCore is now 1 USDC. According to Odaily, transfers below 1 USDC will not be credited to HyperCore.

data.title: ARK Plans 14 Thematic ETFs Covering AI and Tokenized Markets
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, ARK ETF Trust filed registration documents with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for 14 thematic ETFs covering areas including artificial intelligence, robotics, biotechnology and tokenized-market infrastructure. The preliminary prospectus is dated November 6 and is expected to become effective 75 days after filing.

One proposed fund, the ARK Tokenized Market Infrastructure ETF, would invest in companies providing infrastructure for real-world asset tokenization and on-chain capital markets, including tokenization platforms, stablecoin issuers, exchanges, brokers, custodians and settlement networks. The other proposed funds are ARK Neobanks ETF, ARK Agentic Cyber Defense ETF, ARK Neoclouds ETF, ARK Frontier AI Labs ETF, ARK AI Agents ETF, ARK Orbital Data Centers ETF, ARK Robotaxis ETF, ARK Humanoid Robots & Physical AI ETF, ARK Brain Computer Interfaces & Surgical Robotics ETF, ARK Longevity ETF, ARK Peptides ETF, ARK AI Factory ETF and ARK Functional Cures ETF. Tickers have not been determined, and the SEC has neither approved nor rejected the securities.

data.title: China’s NDRC Cites Weak Demand as Economic Challenge
data.description: China’s National Development and Reform Commission flagged weak demand as a challenge as policymakers study measures for next year, Bloomberg reported, citing a statement Friday.

data.title: Rosstat System Recovery After Cyberattack Delays Economic Reports Through Nov. 13
data.description: Russia’s Rosstat is struggling to restore systems after a major cyberattack, delaying major economic reports through at least Nov. 13, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: SoftBank, ABB Explore China Carve-Out to Revive Robotics Deal
data.description: SoftBank Group Corp. and ABB Ltd. are considering carving out the Chinese portion of a major robotics deal blocked by Beijing as they seek to salvage the transaction, according to people familiar with the matter, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: ECB Candidate de Cos Urges Vigilance on Inflation Risks
data.description: Pablo Hernández de Cos, one of two candidates to replace Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president, said policymakers should remain alert to inflation risks from high energy prices, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Trafigura Buys Copper in Asia as China Faces Supply Shortage
data.description: Trafigura Group has been buying large volumes of copper to increase sales in Asia as local supplies dwindle, according to Bloomberg. The buying adds to a scramble for metal that has pushed regional premiums for spot cargoes to record highs.

data.title: Magnificent Seven Lose About $1.04 Trillion in a Day as AI Spending Pressures Big Tech Cash Flow
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing SemiAnalysis, U.S. technology stocks sold off sharply after the midterm elections amid concerns about tighter AI regulation and slower data-center construction. On November 5, the Magnificent Seven lost about $1.04 trillion in market value. Nvidia fell 9.26%, shedding more than $440 billion in market value—two to four times the declines of major customers Microsoft, Google and Amazon.

Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta generated a combined operating cash flow that no longer covered capital expenditures in the third quarter, leaving a shortfall of about $26.4 billion, compared with a surplus of about $61.7 billion a year earlier. Amazon’s trailing 12-month free cash flow swung from a $14.8 billion inflow to a $42.4 billion outflow. Meta’s free cash flow turned negative for the first time in more than a decade, while Google’s long-term debt rose from about $20 billion to $125 billion.

On Election Day, 40 of 41 local ballot measures concerning data centers across 10 states favored restrictions; 27 restrictive or opposition measures passed. SemiAnalysis said the policy changes may have limited impact on projects already underway in 2027 but could affect computing-capacity expansion plans from 2028 onward. More than 90% of Nvidia’s revenue comes from data centers. Meanwhile, Google Cloud’s third-quarter operating profit tripled year over year, AWS operating profit rose from $11.4 billion to $17.8 billion, and Microsoft Azure revenue grew 48%.

data.title: Kalshi and Polymarket Election Markets Top $3 Billion in 2026 Midterm Trading
data.description: Markets related to Kalshi and Polymarket recorded more than $3 billion in combined trading volume during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. According to PANews, Kalshi reported an accuracy rate of about 98% and said it reached a 99% probability on a key race roughly 115 minutes before CNN; its politics category had $679.2 million in open interest, while sports markets recorded $1.5 billion in volume, nearly 60% of the total. The report noted that sample dilution and errors in estimating seat margins remained.

data.title: DeepSeek Says It Has Fixed Partial Web and API Outage
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing STAR Market Daily, DeepSeek’s web and API services experienced a partial outage starting at 3:11 PM today, with users temporarily unable to access its chat function. The affected services included chat, the DeepSeek V4 Pro API, and the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash API. DeepSeek said it had implemented a fix and was monitoring its effectiveness.

data.title: U.S. Democratic Lawmakers Plan Legislation to Repeal Trump Tariffs
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, several Democratic members of Congress say they will work to repeal current tariffs they consider unreasonable, as voters react strongly to high living costs and inflation. Representatives Richard Neal and Ron Wyden are among those planning to pursue legislation next year to reverse the Trump administration’s tariff policies.

data.title: U.S. October CPI in Focus as Markets Weigh December Rate Hike Prospects
data.description: U.S. inflation data due next week will be closely watched as investors assess whether persistent price pressures could prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again in December. However, growing concerns over the AI investment boom and its potential impact on economic growth add uncertainty to the policy outlook.The Bureau of Labor Statistics is scheduled to release October's Consumer Price Index (CPI) report on Tuesday, November 10. The data will be followed by October's Producer Price Index (PPI) report on Friday, as well as speeches from Fed officials.According to a market analysis published by Seeking Alpha, consensus expectations point to a 0.3% monthly increase in headline CPI and a 0.2% rise in core CPI, excluding food and energy. Annual headline inflation is expected to remain at 3.7%, while core inflation could ease to 2.5% from 2.6% in September.However, recent economic surveys suggest inflation could come in hotter than expected. October's ISM Manufacturing and Services Prices Paid indexes both stood at 73, indicating persistent cost pressures across the two sectors. S&P Global's October PMI surveys also showed that selling prices for goods and services rose at their fastest pace since August 2022.Businesses cited higher energy and fuel costs, tariffs, raw material shortages, freight expenses and wages as contributing factors.Housing inflation is another area to watch. According to Zillow's latest forecast, annual rent inflation could reach approximately 3.1% by the end of 2026, while owners' equivalent rent could approach 3.4%. The stabilization and potential recovery in rents could limit further declines in shelter inflation.December Rate Hike ExpectationsStronger inflation and recent employment data have strengthened expectations for another Fed rate increase. According to LSEG data cited by Dow Jones Newswires on November 6, money markets were pricing in a 75% probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December 9 meeting.Nick Rees, head of macro research at Monex, said that without a significant downside surprise in the October CPI report or the November jobs report due December 4, a December rate hike could become almost fully priced in before the meeting.ING analysts also expect both headline and core CPI to rise 0.3% month over month in October, a reading that could further support the case for tighter monetary policy.AI Investment Risks Add to Market UncertaintyDespite the renewed focus on inflation, the outlook for technology investment could also influence market expectations for Fed policy.In a November 6 analysis, Seeking Alpha contributor Damir Tokic argued that concerns over a potential AI investment bubble could eventually outweigh backward-looking inflation data. He pointed to credit concerns surrounding CoreWeave and developments in China's semiconductor industry as signs of growing pressure on the sector.A broader pullback in AI infrastructure spending could weigh on business investment and economic growth, potentially increasing recession risks and shifting the Fed's attention toward monetary easing.For now, however, the October CPI report remains a key near-term catalyst. A stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce expectations of a December rate hike, while weaker data may ease pressure on the Fed. Investors will also monitor energy prices and developments in the AI sector as they assess the outlook for equities, bonds and cryptocurrencies.

data.title: U.S. Port Labor Talks Extended Through November 20
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, a union representing about 250 security workers at the busiest U.S. port agreed to extend negotiations for a new labor contract by two weeks, through November 20. The Pacific Maritime Association said talks with International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 will continue to avoid an operational disruption that could affect about 85% of cargo at the Port of Long Beach and roughly one-third at the Port of Los Angeles.

data.title: Hong Kong SFC to Expand Restricted Titles List and Speed Up Updates
data.description: Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission said it will expand its list of restricted titles and establish a mechanism to update it more quickly. According to Odaily, the proposed amendments received broad market support, and regulatory coverage will also extend to virtual assets.

data.description: On Polymarket, the “Map 1 Winner” option for TheMongolz in the “Counter-Strike: TheMongolz vs. Natus Vincere - IEM Beijing Playoffs” event climbed to 69.5%, up from 33.5% one hour earlier, a 36% increase. data.title: Taiwan Temple Abbot and Son Accused of Embezzling Nearly 70 Million Yuan and Laundering Funds Through Crypto
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Observer Network, Zhang Qingyu, abbot of Donglin Temple in Yilan, Taiwan, and his son Zhang Weifu, who has become a monk, are suspected of embezzling donations. During a search, investigators reportedly dug more than 10 iron chests containing gold and silver from gravel outside the meditation room; the metals were valued at more than 330 million New Taiwan dollars, or about 70 million yuan. Investigators said temple funds were transferred to private accounts and laundered through purchases of cryptocurrency, gold, and silver. The investigation is ongoing.

data.title: Los Angeles Port Strike Threat Delayed as Labor Talks Get Two-Week Extension
data.description: A potential strike at the Port of Los Angeles was deferred again after the union representing about 250 security workers at the busiest US ports agreed to continue labor contract negotiations for two more weeks, employers said, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI TRENDS | UK Growth Minister Dan Tomlinson: Britain Will Not Slow AI Development Despite U.S. Backlash
data.description: UK Growth Minister Dan Tomlinson said Britain would not slow its AI development despite a backlash against AI emerging in the United States during the midterm elections. According to Sina Finance, Tomlinson said in an interview that Britain should not assume it would replicate the polarized debate in the United States. Democratic candidates won major victories with campaign platforms that included tighter regulation and slower data center construction. Tomlinson said Britain could avoid a fierce debate over data centers and continue treating them as critical infrastructure. He added that the government had observed disorderly development in some parts of the United States and learned from it. He said Britain was taking a different approach, and its regulatory framework already included some of the oversight mechanisms sought by the victorious Democratic candidates.

data.title: STOCKS | South Korean Stocks Fall as Retail Investors’ Five-Day U.S. Stock Buying Exceeds August Total
data.description:
South Korean stocks fell as retail investors increased their U.S. stock purchases, with five trading days of net buying exceeding the total for August. According to Sina Finance, citing data released by the Korea Securities Depository’s SEIBro platform on the 7th, investors net bought $2.19753 billion in U.S. stocks from the 2nd through the 6th, equivalent to about 2.982 trillion won. That was more than August’s $1.96234 billion and over twice September’s $1.00128 billion, and equaled about 40% of the previous month’s $5.42312 billion total. During the same five sessions, investors net bought 4.2 trillion won in shares on the KOSPI main board, nearly matching their U.S. stock purchases.

South Korean retail investors were net sellers of U.S. stocks in April and May, selling $468.93 million and $939.77 million, respectively. They turned to net buying in June and continued increasing purchases, with last month’s net buying reaching an 11-month high. The shift came as South Korean stocks retreated after failing to extend their gains from the first half of the year and the won strengthened from the 1,500-per-dollar range to the mid-1,300s, lowering the cost of converting won into dollars.

Purchases were concentrated in Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares (SOXL), which seeks three times the daily return of a semiconductor index. Investors net bought $1.62525 billion of SOXL from the 2nd through the 6th, more than 70% of total net U.S. stock purchases. They also net bought $497.05 million of Alphabet shares and $220.22 million of ProShares UltraPro QQQ (TQQQ), which seeks three times the daily return of the Nasdaq-100 Index.

According to the Korea Financial Investment Association, brokerage investor deposit balances stood at 88.5338 trillion won as of the 5th, remaining below 100 trillion won for nearly a month since the 13th of last month. Margin debt was around 28 trillion won, at 28.7715 trillion won.
